name: Crobh Dearg

attributes.attribute: an Irish goddess of the southwestern province of Munster
sometimes said to be the sister of Latiaran

sources: MacNeill, Máire. The Festival of Lughnasa. Parts I and II. Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982. Pp. 272-274.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Crobh Dearg, also written Crove Derg, was a goddess of Ireland. She held sway in Munster, the province in the southwest. Her title translates as red claw. A few accounts call her the sister of Latiaran, a deity reshaped for Christianity.

okr.objective: Crobh Dearg is an Irish goddess of Munster whose name means “red claw.”
key_results: She was an Irish goddess of the southwestern province of Munster.
Some accounts name her the sister of Latiaran, a Christianized god.
